learning_goal: Build every pharyngeal arch from the same five ingredients, then name for arches 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 the cartilage, the muscles, the cranial nerve and the artery, and use that one table to explain the course of both recurrent laryngeal nerves and the first-arch, second-arch and neural crest syndromes.

model.t_meaning: t = 0 is day 22; t = 1 is day 56. day(t) = 22 + 34t.

structures.name: Pharyngeal foregut
structures.label: Pharyngeal foregut
structures.narration: The bars are arranged round the side wall of the pharynx, so the foregut is the thing to find first: every arch is a bar on its wall, every cleft a groove outside it and every pouch a recess inside it.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 1
structures.label: Arch 1 — the mandibular arch: chewing, and two ear ossicles
structures.narration: Arch one splits into a maxillary and a mandibular prominence and builds the jaws. Its cartilage is Meckel's cartilage, and its fate is worth stating precisely: the dorsal end becomes the malleus and incus, the middle becomes the anterior ligament of the malleus and the sphenomandibular ligament, and the rest is resorbed while the mandible ossifies in membrane beside it. The mandible is not Meckel's cartilage turned to bone. Its muscles are the four muscles of mastication plus mylohyoid, the anterior belly of digastric, tensor tympani and tensor veli palatini. Nerve, trigeminal. Artery, the maxillary.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 2
structures.label: Arch 2 — the hyoid arch: the face that smiles
structures.narration: Arch two is the hyoid arch and its cartilage is Reichert's. From it come the stapes, the styloid process, the stylohyoid ligament, and the lesser horn and upper body of the hyoid. Its muscles are all the muscles of facial expression, plus stapedius, stylohyoid and the posterior belly of digastric — which is exactly the motor territory of the facial nerve. Arch two also overgrows arches three and four, burying them in a space called the cervical sinus. Remember that overgrowth: it is where the branchial cyst comes from.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 3
structures.label: Arch 3 — one muscle, one nerve, half a hyoid
structures.narration: Arch three is the easiest to learn because it has one of everything. Its cartilage gives the greater horn and the lower body of the hyoid — so the hyoid is a two-arch bone, upper half from arch two and lower half from arch three. Its only muscle is stylopharyngeus and its nerve is the glossopharyngeal. Its artery becomes the common carotid and the first part of the internal carotid.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 4
structures.label: Arch 4 — swallowing, and one laryngeal muscle
structures.narration: Arch four builds the thyroid and epiglottic cartilages, the three pharyngeal constrictors, levator veli palatini and one laryngeal muscle, the cricothyroid. Its nerve is the superior laryngeal branch of the vagus, and the external laryngeal branch of it runs with the superior thyroid artery — which is why cricothyroid is the muscle at risk in thyroid surgery and why the injured patient loses the top of the voice rather than the whole of it. Its artery is the arch of the aorta on the left and the right subclavian artery on the right.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 5
structures.label: Arch 5 — the one that never counts
structures.narration: There is no fifth arch to learn. In the human it either never forms or regresses as soon as it appears, and it leaves no cartilage, no muscle, no nerve and no artery. Say the surviving arches out loud as one, two, three, four and six, and the missing number stops being a trap in the question.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 6
structures.label: Arch 6 — the voice
structures.narration: Arch six gives the cricoid, arytenoid, corniculate and cuneiform cartilages and every intrinsic muscle of the larynx except the cricothyroid, which belonged to arch four. Its nerve is therefore the recurrent laryngeal branch of the vagus. Its artery becomes the proximal pulmonary artery on both sides, and on the left it also leaves the ductus arteriosus.

structures.name: Pharyngeal clefts
structures.label: Clefts — the grooves outside
structures.narration: The ectodermal grooves between the bars. They are named here only so the bars read as separate: the clefts, the tympanic membrane and the cervical sinus remnants belong to the Pharyngeal clefts & membranes entry.

structures.name: Pharyngeal pouches
structures.label: Pouches — the recesses inside
structures.narration: The endodermal recesses facing the clefts from inside. Thymus, parathyroids, tonsil and the tubotympanic recess belong to the Pharyngeal pouches entry and are deliberately absent here.

structures.name: Arch 1 cartilage
structures.label: Arch 1 — Meckel's cartilage
structures.narration: The skeletal element of arch 1, built by neural crest in the core of its own bar. It carries arch 1’s colour in every beat, because the whole point is that the cartilage, the muscle, the nerve and the artery all belong to the same numbered block.

structures.name: Arch 2 cartilage
structures.label: Arch 2 — Reichert's cartilage
structures.narration: The skeletal element of arch 2, built by neural crest in the core of its own bar. It carries arch 2’s colour in every beat, because the whole point is that the cartilage, the muscle, the nerve and the artery all belong to the same numbered block.

structures.name: Arch 3 cartilage
structures.label: Arch 3 — greater horn & lower body of hyoid
structures.narration: The skeletal element of arch 3, built by neural crest in the core of its own bar. It carries arch 3’s colour in every beat, because the whole point is that the cartilage, the muscle, the nerve and the artery all belong to the same numbered block.

structures.name: Arch 4 cartilage
structures.label: Arch 4 — thyroid & epiglottic cartilage
structures.narration: The skeletal element of arch 4, built by neural crest in the core of its own bar. It carries arch 4’s colour in every beat, because the whole point is that the cartilage, the muscle, the nerve and the artery all belong to the same numbered block.

structures.name: Arch 6 cartilage
structures.label: Arch 6 — cricoid, arytenoid, corniculate, cuneiform
structures.narration: The skeletal element of arch 6, built by neural crest in the core of its own bar. It carries arch 6’s colour in every beat, because the whole point is that the cartilage, the muscle, the nerve and the artery all belong to the same numbered block.

structures.name: Aortic sac
structures.label: Aortic sac
structures.narration: Each arch is fed by an artery running from the aortic sac to the dorsal aorta, and the adult pattern is what survives after selective regression. Arch one leaves part of the maxillary artery, arch two the small stapedial artery, arch three the common carotid and the start of the internal carotid, arch four the aortic arch on the left and the right subclavian on the right, arch six the pulmonary arteries with the ductus arteriosus on the left. The right side loses more than the left, and that asymmetry is the whole explanation of the next point.

structures.name: Dorsal aortae
structures.label: Dorsal aortae
structures.narration: Each arch artery runs from the sac to the dorsal aorta of its own side. The two fuse caudally, and the part of the left one below the fourth arch becomes the descending aorta the left recurrent nerve ends up beside.

structures.name: First arch artery
structures.label: First arch artery — maxillary stub
structures.narration: Arch artery 1. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Second arch artery
structures.label: Second arch artery — stapedial stub
structures.narration: Arch artery 2. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Third arch artery, right
structures.label: Third arch artery, right — common & internal carotid
structures.narration: Arch artery 3, right side. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Third arch artery, left
structures.label: Third arch artery, left — common & internal carotid
structures.narration: Arch artery 3, left side. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Fourth arch artery, right
structures.label: Fourth arch artery, right — right subclavian
structures.narration: Arch artery 4, right side. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Fourth arch artery, left
structures.label: Fourth arch artery, left — arch of the aorta
structures.narration: Arch artery 4, left side. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Fifth arch artery
structures.label: Fifth arch artery — leaves nothing
structures.narration: Arch artery 5. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Sixth arch artery, right
structures.label: Sixth arch artery, right — right pulmonary artery
structures.narration: Arch artery 6, right side. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Sixth arch artery, left
structures.label: Sixth arch artery, left — pulmonary artery & ductus arteriosus
structures.narration: Arch artery 6, left side. What survives of it is the adult derivative named in its label; the rest regresses, and the pattern of what is left is what the next two beats are about.

structures.name: Trigeminal nerve
structures.label: V — trigeminal: arch 1
structures.narration: The nerve of arch one, running in arch one’s core with the muscles of mastication.

structures.name: Facial nerve
structures.label: VII — facial: arch 2
structures.narration: The nerve of arch two. Everything it supplies came from one arch, which is why one lesion takes the whole face, taste from the front of the tongue and the stapedius reflex together.

structures.name: Glossopharyngeal nerve
structures.label: IX — glossopharyngeal: arch 3
structures.narration: The nerve of arch three, and the reason stylopharyngeus — alone among the pharyngeal muscles — answers to the glossopharyngeal.

structures.name: Vagus nerve
structures.label: X — vagus: arches 4 and 6
structures.narration: The vagus claims both of the surviving caudal arches, through two different branches: the superior laryngeal for arch four and the recurrent laryngeal for arch six.

structures.name: Superior laryngeal nerve
structures.label: Superior laryngeal — arch 4
structures.narration: Arch four’s branch of the vagus. Its external laryngeal branch runs with the superior thyroid artery, which is why cricothyroid is the muscle at risk in thyroid surgery.

structures.name: Right recurrent laryngeal nerve
structures.label: Right recurrent laryngeal — hooks arch 4
structures.narration: On the right the sixth arch artery’s distal part regresses, so nothing holds this nerve there and it rides up to the fourth — the right subclavian. Its course is short, and a right vocal cord palsy is almost always a lesion in the neck.

structures.name: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve
structures.label: Left recurrent laryngeal — hooks arch 6
structures.narration: The nerve of arch six is caught under the artery of arch six on each side. On the right, the fifth and sixth arch arteries regress, so the nerve slips up until it is caught by the next artery still standing — the fourth, which is the right subclavian. On the left the sixth arch artery persists as the ductus arteriosus, so the nerve stays hooked around it and is dragged into the chest as the heart descends. That is why a left vocal cord palsy sends you looking at the lung apex, the aortic arch and the mediastinal nodes, and why a right-sided one is almost always in the neck.

structures.name: Heart
structures.label: The heart, descending
structures.narration: The heart starts in the neck and descends into the thorax through weeks five to eight. It is here because it is the thing that tows the left nerve down: the sac, the sixth arch artery and the hook all follow it.

structures.name: Ectoderm
structures.label: Ectoderm — outside
structures.narration: Ectoderm covers the arch on its outer surface. It is the layer the clefts are grooves in.

structures.name: Endoderm
structures.label: Endoderm — inside
structures.narration: Endoderm lines the arch on the surface facing the pharynx. It is the layer the pouches are recesses in.

structures.name: Core
structures.label: Core — mesoderm and neural crest
structures.narration: Ectoderm covers the arch outside, endoderm lines it inside, and the core is filled by mesoderm invaded by neural crest cells. The division of labour is exact and it is examinable. Neural crest builds the skeleton and the connective tissue of the arch. Paraxial mesoderm builds the muscles. That is why a neural crest disorder wrecks the face and the jaw while the muscles that move them are still innervated normally.

structures.name: Cartilage
structures.label: Cartilage — neural crest
structures.narration: The skeletal element, built by neural crest, lying in the centre of the core.

structures.name: Muscle
structures.label: Muscle — paraxial mesoderm
structures.narration: The muscle block, built by paraxial mesoderm, superficial to the cartilage in the core.

structures.name: The arch nerve
structures.label: The arch nerve
structures.narration: Each arch is claimed by one cranial nerve: the fifth for arch one, the seventh for arch two, the ninth for arch three, the tenth for arches four and six. The muscle of an arch may migrate a long way from where it started, but it keeps the nerve it was born with. That single rule is why the stapedius deep in the middle ear is supplied by the facial nerve and why the stylopharyngeus, alone among the pharyngeal muscles, answers to the glossopharyngeal.

structures.name: The arch artery
structures.label: The arch artery
structures.narration: The arch artery, the deepest of the three things flanking the cartilage, running from the aortic sac to the dorsal aorta.

structures.name: Cervical sinus
structures.label: Cervical sinus — the buried space
structures.narration: Arch two overgrows the arches below it, and the clefts it buries are left as this space. It should obliterate in week seven.

structures.name: Branchial cyst
structures.label: Branchial cyst — when it does not close
structures.narration: Two things follow from arch two. First, everything the facial nerve supplies came from one arch, so a single nerve lesion takes the whole face, taste from the front of the tongue and the stapedius reflex together — which is why hyperacusis belongs in a facial palsy history. Second, arch two overgrows the arches below it and the buried space, the cervical sinus, should disappear. When it does not, a branchial cyst appears in the young adult at the anterior border of sternocleidomastoid. The cyst is a cleft remnant, not an arch derivative, and this scene names it only so it is not learned twice.

structures.name: Arch 1, under-built
structures.label: Arch 1 under-built — too little neural crest
structures.narration: Too few neural crest cells reach arch one and the whole arch is under-built. In Treacher Collins syndrome the cheekbones and mandible are hypoplastic, the palpebral fissures slant downwards, the lower lid is notched, the external ear is malformed and the hearing loss is conductive because the ossicles came from the same arch. In the Pierre Robin sequence a small mandible pushes the tongue back and up, which both obstructs the airway and blocks the palatal shelves from meeting — one primary defect, three consequences in a chain. The neonatal problem is the airway, not the cleft.

structures.name: Pharyngeal arch 1
structures.label: Arch 1 — the bar it lies in
structures.narration: The same bar as arch 1, drawn translucent so that what lies in its core — the cartilage, the nerve and the artery — can be seen inside it rather than behind it. It carries arch 1’s colour, like everything else that belongs to arch 1.

views.title: Six bars on the side of the neck
views.narration: Look at the week four embryo from the side. The head is bent over a series of bars stacked one above the other on the side of the pharynx, separated outside by clefts and inside by pouches. Six pairs form. Count them from the top and remember that the fifth is not there to be counted.

views.narration: Cut one arch across and the plan is visible in a single picture. Ectoderm on the outside, endoderm on the inside, and in the core a cartilage bar, a muscle mass, a nerve and an artery. Neural crest makes the bar and the connective tissue, mesoderm makes the muscle. The nerve belongs to the muscle and never lets go of it.

views.title: Fill the table, arch by arch
views.narration: Now go down the series once and fill four columns for each arch. One: Meckel's cartilage, malleus and incus, the muscles of mastication, the trigeminal. Two: Reichert's cartilage, stapes and styloid, the muscles of facial expression, the facial. Three: greater horn of hyoid, stylopharyngeus, the glossopharyngeal. Four: thyroid cartilage, the constrictors and cricothyroid, the superior laryngeal branch of the vagus. Six: the remaining laryngeal cartilages and all the other intrinsic laryngeal muscles, the recurrent laryngeal branch of the vagus. Five: nothing. Notice the hyoid is shared between arches two and three, and the larynx between arches four and six.

views.title: One arch fails, and you can predict the child

ops.kind: too few neural crest cells under-build it, and the arch below overgrows into

views.narration: Hang a syndrome on each arch. Arch one under-built: Treacher Collins, with a small jaw, a malformed ear and conductive deafness, or the Pierre Robin sequence where the small mandible obstructs the airway and blocks the palate. Arch two: the facial nerve territory taken as one, and a branchial cyst from the cervical sinus. Arches three and four with the heart's outflow: the twenty-two q eleven deletion. The pattern to carry into the exam is that arch defects and conotruncal heart defects travel together, because they are the same cells failing.

deferred_beats.title: One body plan, repeated six times
deferred_beats.narration: In week four the future head and neck are six pairs of bars running round the side wall of the pharynx. Do not memorise them as six separate things. Every arch is built to the same plan: a cartilage bar, a block of muscle, one cranial nerve and one artery, wrapped in ectoderm outside and endoderm inside. Learn the plan once, then fill in five columns of a table.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: It states the plan in words and draws nothing that the beats either side of it do not already draw: view 1 shows the six bars and view 2 cuts one across to show the plan itself, so a third frame between them would be the same picture twice. RENDER-STANDARD: "A VIEW MUST CHANGE THE PICTURE ... Move them to deferred_beats[] with their full narration."
deferred_beats.where_it_belongs: spoken over view 1, as the opening statement of the topic

deferred_beats.title: When the crest fails everywhere at once
deferred_beats.narration: Neural crest cells serve the arches and the outflow tract of the heart, so one failure produces defects in both. In the twenty-two q eleven deletion the third and fourth arch territory is under-built: a small jaw and abnormal facies, cleft palate, a conotruncal heart defect such as interrupted aortic arch or truncus arteriosus, and the pouch derivatives missing behind them. When you find an arch defect, examine the heart, and when you find a conotruncal defect, look at the face. Excess retinoic acid does the same thing to the same cells, which is why isotretinoin is not given in pregnancy.
deferred_beats.why_not_a_view: The picture this paragraph needs is the arch territory AND the outflow tract of the heart under-built together — that pairing is its whole argument. This model builds the heart only as a context blob and does not build the conotruncus at all, so the beat could show the arch half and would have to assert the cardiac half in a caption. The model CAN under-build arches 3 and 4 (the deficit_crest34 variant is built and reachable); what is missing is the conotruncal geometry to put beside them.
deferred_beats.where_it_belongs: a view of its own once engine__conotruncal-wedging exists, or the Cardiovascular Development topic; spoken over view 6 until then

gaps: CONVERTED FROM THE SVG SEQUENCE ENGINE TO THE PROCEDURAL 3D MODEL on 2026-10-03, and the one thing a reviewer should check first is whether that was the right call, because this scene's own gaps[] argued against it in August. It said: "Routed to its FIRST preferred mode, sequence. The curriculum lists sequence then diagram for this structure and no 3d option, so deferred_modes carries diagram only. A 3d re-authoring would be defensible the day a provider holds staged pharyngeal-region geometry, but the curriculum does not ask for it and this scene does not claim it." CURRICULUM.json still says preferred_modes: [sequence, diagram] for Pharyngeal arches, with no 3d_anatomy. Three things decided it the other way. (1) BUILD-QUEUE.json names this item explicitly as one of the 28 SVG-panel scenes to re-author, with the note "six arches as bars. Separated solids — should be a clean one". (2) model3d-scene-spec-v2.md is explicit that the list is not a ceiling: "A structure routed to diagram becomes a 3D scene the day a model for it exists, with no curriculum edit — which is the point: today's provider coverage must never harden into a permanent curriculum rule." (3) The precedent is settled: embryology__gametogenesis-fertilization__blastocyst has the IDENTICAL curriculum entry (preferred_modes [sequence, diagram], no 3d) and was converted to mode 3d_anatomy with provider procedural, and is marked `done` in the queue — reviewed by a session that did not build it, and passed. The deciding fact is that the old scene was status:'planned' and NOTHING RENDERED: no SVG artwork for it exists or was ever drawn, so a student saw nothing at all. The curriculum's two declared view types, location and associated_organs, are both delivered here (views 1, 3 and 6), and sequence and diagram are kept on the record in deferred_modes.

THE ARCH BARS ARE SMOOTH CRESCENTS OF CONSTANT SECTION, round in cross-section and tapering only towards their dorsal ends. A real arch is an irregular prominence, and arch 1 in particular splits into a maxillary and a mandibular process which this model does not build — arch1's own narration names that split and the picture does not show it. Declared rather than attempted, because the split is the subject of the 'Facial prominences' curriculum entry, which this scene does not claim.

NO MUSCLE BLOCKS ON THE WHOLE-SERIES MODEL. The five ingredients appear together only on the magnified section (view 2), where the muscle is sec_muscle. On the series itself the model builds the cartilage, the nerve and the artery in each arch core but not the muscle mass, so a beat that wanted to show the muscles of mastication inside arch 1 could not. The muscle derivatives are taught by name in each arch's narration instead.

NO SURFACE ECTODERM OVER THE SERIES. The ectodermal covering is taught on the section, where it is legible. A translucent closed shell over the whole embryo would have bought the self-occlusion artefact RENDER-STANDARD 3.ac describes for no teaching gain.

THE HYOID IS NOT SHOWN AS ONE BONE. Arch 3's narration makes the examinable point that "the hyoid is a two-arch bone, upper half from arch two and lower half from arch three", and the model does not draw the two halves meeting. Measured: cart2's caudal end and cart3's cranial end are 0.275 apart against a mean y extent of 0.297 — a gap of 0.93 of their own size. It cannot be closed by nudging them, because each cartilage is built inside its own arch and the arches are 0.54 apart in y while an arch bar's thickness lets its cartilage move about 0.13 of that. Acceptance row M therefore asserts the half of the claim the model can carry (cart2 lies wholly cranial to cart3 — upper from arch 2, lower from arch 3, floored at 0.35 of their mean extent) and deliberately does NOT assert that they meet. The narration keeps the sentence, per RENDER-STANDARD: editing a teaching sentence to agree with an approximate model "teaches something false about the body in order to make a check go green". THE FIX, for whoever takes this next: a `hyoid` structure of its own, built as one bone in two colours, with cart2 and cart3 ending on it.

TWO VESTIGE FLOORS, AND NEITHER IS A CLAIM THAT ANYTHING PERSISTS. Arch 5 and the fifth arch artery leave nothing in the human — arch5's own narration says so in as many words. The honest size for both at t = 1 is zero, but a key that builds no triangles comes back from the procedural adapter as reason:'none', which viz3d shows a student as "there is no model of this structure": a confident lie about a model sitting right there. So both floor at 8.5% and 6% of full size. The floors are NOT shown to a student anywhere: THREE keys pin their refs to day 30 — arch5, aa5 AND arch5_ghost — that being the one day on which the fifth arch and its artery exist. arch5 and aa5 are shown only by views 1 and 4. arch5_ghost is reached by view 3’s group show of “Arch ghosts”, which is why view 3 hides it by name: REVIEWED 2026-10-03, that hide was missing and view 3 drew a full-size day-30 arch 5 bar at day 38 under narration reading “Five: nothing”. An enumeration of pinned keys that omits one is how this survived the build; keep all three named here. Acceptance row F asserts arch 5 is at least 3x larger at its peak than at t = 1, and the claimMeasure `archCount` returns 6 only at day 30 and 5 at every later t, which is the beat-level expression of the same fact.

THE PHARYNGEAL AXIS IS SMOOTH AND THE ARCHES ARE EVENLY DROOPED. The cervical flexure is modelled as a single cubic bend and every arch droops by the same amount reaching the ventral midline, so the series is more regular than a real embryo's. That regularity is what makes the six bars countable, which is view 1's whole job, and it is the kind of regularisation a teaching diagram makes too.

SIDE CLAIMS ARE PROVEN, WHICH IS NOT THE DEFAULT FOR A PROCEDURAL MODEL. RENDER-STANDARD's rule "A DECLARED AXIS IS NOT A PROVED ONE, AND A SYMMETRIC MODEL CANNOT PROVE ITS OWN" would otherwise leave every left/right claim here unproven — and the left/right asymmetry of the two recurrent laryngeal nerves is the payoff of view 5. Both routes that rule allows are taken: (b) the declared axes string is checked against the scan data by viz-training/tools/prove-corpus-axes.mjs, which measures the convention off six BodyParts3D right/left mesh pairs and now reports pharyngeal-arches.js as agreeing with it; and (a) acceptance row A measures the right-hand members of the per-side artery pairs out of the BUILT geometry at negative x with a 0.35 magnitude floor. Row K is the one that makes it bite: before the regression the two hooks sit level to within 7% of the nerves' own extent and BOTH hook arch 6, so the asymmetry cannot have been written into the nerves — it is produced by archArteryKeep and by nothing else. A model with two hand-placed hook heights passes rows H, I and J and fails K.

BEATS 3 AND 4 DRAW THE ARCH BARS AS TRANSLUCENT GHOSTS (the 'Arch ghosts' group: the same six model parts, authored at opacity 0.28 under their own keys), and that is a fix the visibility walk forced rather than a decoration. A cartilage and an arch artery both lie INSIDE their arch's core — that is the anatomy, and it is why the no-shared-space row excludes those pairs by name — so a beat that draws the bars opaque shows a student the bars and nothing else: the walk measured all five cartilages at 0.000% of beat 3's frame. Hiding the bars instead made the cartilages visible and the beat BADLY FRAMED, at 4.52% of frame against an 8% floor, because five thin curved rods in a tall box are mostly empty picture. The ghosts solve both: the contents are seen through the bar they belong to, which is the teaching, and the bar's own ink gives the frame a subject. The opacity is MEASURED and not chosen by eye — RENDER-STANDARD 3.ab corollary 1, 'a translucency chosen by eye is a guess; render it and count' — and the walk's per-beat figures for every ghosted structure are in viz-training/models-out/pharyngeal-arches/player/visibility.json. viz3d sets depthWrite = opacity >= 0.98, so a ghost does not fill the depth buffer in front of what it contains.

BEAT 6 HIDES arch5 AND aa5 EXPLICITLY, and that is a defect the beat-claim check found rather than tidiness. Both pin their refs to day 30 (see the vestige-floor note above), and viz3d cannot restage a pinned ref — SET_STAGE returns null for one (viz3d.js:561) — so a beat at day 44 that left them showing would draw a FULL-SIZE fifth arch and its artery in a week-seven picture, which is the one thing this scene exists to tell a student does not happen. The other nineteen reports of the same shape in that run were the TOOL mis-modelling visibility rather than the scene: viz-training/tools/check-beat-claims.mjs resolved a target naming a GROUP as though it were a structure key, and did not implement ISOLATE_REGION or PEEL_LAYER at all, so it believed every structure in a hidden group was still on screen. Fixed in that file the same day with the reason written there; re-run on blastocyst, cardiac-cycle-pumping and notochord it gives byte-identical results before and after, so the change is a no-op on every other scene this run could test.

THE ARCH COLOUR KEY IS IDENTICAL IN EVERY BEAT, which the August scene asked for and which is now enforced by the scene rather than by a drawer's care: cart1..cart6 carry the SAME hex as arch1..arch6 (the scene's colour overrides the model's own lighter palette — viz3d.js load()), and the per-side arteries carry tints of their own arch's colour. The entire teaching point is that cartilage, muscle, nerve, artery and syndrome all belong to the same numbered block.

VIEW 5 DRAWS THE LEFT AND RIGHT SIDES TOGETHER, from the anterior camera, which the August scene required: "The artery panel must draw the left and right sides together, not one generic side. The asymmetry of the two recurrent laryngeal nerves is the payoff of the beat and it is invisible on a single-sided drawing."

BEAT 3 TRACES concept:arch-series. The subject is a progression through the series rather than a drawn region, so the trace walks the five cartilages in order; the procedural adapter degrades TRACE_STRUCTURE to a timed sequential highlight along the path, which is what the beat wants anyway.

VIEW 6 AUTHORS PEEL_LAYER on the vessel layer to take the arch arteries off the clinical picture after views 4 and 5 have used them. The renderer degrades it to hiding structures tagged with that layer; the op is authored because the arteries are needed to explain the nerves and then clutter the clinical panel.

'Pharyngeal pouches', 'Pharyngeal clefts & membranes', 'Thyroid gland development', 'Facial prominences' and 'Palate formation' are NOT claimed in covers[]. The clefts and pouches are built as CONTEXT so that view 1's narration — "separated outside by clefts and inside by pouches" — points at something a student can see, and each carries narration saying what belongs to the other entries. The cervical sinus and the branchial cyst appear in the clinical beat because the overgrowth that buries them is an arch event, but the clefts themselves, the tympanic membrane and the full account of cervical sinus remnants belong to that entry.

AORTIC ARCH ARTERY REMODELLING is taught here only as far as it explains the arch derivatives and the two recurrent laryngeal nerves. The double aortic arch, the aberrant right subclavian artery and coarctation belong with the Cardiovascular Development topic and appear here in match.terms only, so a highlighted term still reaches this scene until those exist.

WEEK NUMBERS are the standard teaching approximations — arches appearing through week four, the fifth arch transient around day 30, the cervical sinus obliterating in week seven, the heart descending through weeks five to eight. Texts differ by several days. The model makes them exact because it has to put the geometry somewhere; t is day 22 + 34t and the mapping is stated in scene.model.t_meaning.
SYNDROMES are named with their embryological mechanism and their classic presentation only. Management is paediatrics and surgery, not embryology, and is deliberately absent.

WHAT IS NOT YET MEASURED: this scene has not been through a review round. The build run's own checks are listed in BUILD-LOG.md and in models3d/pharyngeal-arches.js's acceptance block; what nobody other than the builder has looked at is whether the six beats teach what they claim to.
